title: Generic structure-sheaf direct image in equal dimension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Y$ be nonempty integral schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $\dim X=\dim Y=g<\infty$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $g\geq0$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] with dense image. Let $\eta_X,\eta_Y$ be the generic points [def-sc-generic-point]. Equip the function fields $k(X),k(Y)$ [def-sc-function-field] with the actual inclusion $f^*:k(Y)\to k(X)$ of [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Then this field extension is finite. There exists a nonempty open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $(R^if_*\mathcal O_X)|_U=0$ for every $i>0$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Moreover, the canonical germ map identifies $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_{\eta_Y}$ with $k(X)$ as a $k(Y)$-vector space, with scalar action through $f^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. In particular its dimension over $k(Y)$ is $[k(X):f^*k(Y)]$.

proof.text: Put $K=k(Y)$ and $L=k(X)$, with the $K$-algebra structure on $L$ given by $f^*$. Dominance gives $f(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$ as in [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] the generic local rings are fields, so their maximal ideals are zero and they equal their residue fields. Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] to the whole irreducible closed subsets $X\subset X$ and $Y\subset Y$: $\operatorname{trdeg}_kL=\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=g$. The tower identity and zero-degree criterion in [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower], for the tower induced by the $k$-morphism $f$, give $g=g+\operatorname{trdeg}_KL$. Since $g$ is finite, $\operatorname{trdeg}_KL=0$, hence $L/K$ is algebraic.

Choose an affine open $V\ni\eta_Y$ and an affine open $W\ni\eta_X$ inside $f^{-1}V$. Properness includes local finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. With $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $B=\mathcal O_X(W)$, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] gives $B=A[b_1,\ldots,b_r]$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], the compatible generic germ maps identify $K$ and $L$ with the fraction fields of $A$ and $B$. Thus $L=K(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$: the right side contains $B$ and its fractions, and every generator belongs to $L$. Step 1 makes each $b_i$ algebraic over $K$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] proves $[L:K]<\infty$, including $r=0$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre], the finite extension at $\eta_X\mapsto\eta_Y$ makes $\eta_X$ closed in $X_{\eta_Y}$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] its topology is the subspace topology on $f^{-1}(\eta_Y)$. Every point of $X$ is a specialization of $\eta_X$, since $\overline{\{\eta_X\}}=X$. Therefore every point of this fibre is a specialization of its closed point $\eta_X$, and must equal $\eta_X$. Hence $f^{-1}(\eta_Y)=\{\eta_X\}$.

The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, both finitely generated. Its spectrum is the one-point affine scheme, hence is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], both $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian. The source $X$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], so $f$ is quasi-separated by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Properness includes finite type, which includes quasi-compactness and local finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Now $Y$ has only one irreducible component and its generic fibre is a singleton by Step 3. All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] hold. It supplies a dense open $U$ containing $\eta_Y$ on which $f_U:f^{-1}U\to U$ is finite. In particular $U$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tag 01OY; schemes.tex Tag 01KV; Tag 02NW, lemma-generically-finite (1) implies (4)

proof.text: A finite morphism is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The structure sheaf on $f^{-1}U$ is quasi-coherent: on each affine $\operatorname{Spec}B$ it is $\widetilde B$, which is the condition in [pqf-def-coherent]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] gives $R^if_{U,*}\mathcal O_{f^{-1}U}=0$ for $i>0$. The open-restriction isomorphism [lem-pc-higher-direct-image-open-restriction] identifies this with $(R^if_*\mathcal O_X)|_U$, giving the stated vanishing.

For every open neighbourhood $W$ of $\eta_X$, properness says $f(X\setminus W)$ is closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], by taking the identity base change in universal closedness. Step 3 implies $\eta_Y\notin f(X\setminus W)$. Thus $V_W=Y\setminus f(X\setminus W)$ is an open neighbourhood of $\eta_Y$ and $f^{-1}V_W\subseteq W$. These inverse images therefore refine every open neighbourhood of $\eta_X$.

source.place: Tag 0BET, lemma-intersection-number-and-pullback, generic stalk paragraph; elementary closed-map neighbourhood argument

proof.text: Write $C=(f_*\mathcal O_X)_{\eta_Y}$. Using the germ description in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], define $c:C\to L$ by sending the germ of $s\in\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$ to its germ at $\eta_X$. This is well defined since $f(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$, and respects addition and multiplication by restriction of sections. For surjectivity, represent any element of $L$ on a neighbourhood $W$ of $\eta_X$ and restrict it to $f^{-1}V_W$ from Step 6. For injectivity, a section whose germ at $\eta_X$ is zero vanishes on some open $W\subseteq f^{-1}V$ containing $\eta_X$; its restriction to $f^{-1}(V\cap V_W)$ is zero, so its germ in $C$ is zero. Hence the canonical germ map $c$ is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0078, section-stalks, germ equality; explicit application of Step 6

proof.text: The scalar structure on $C$ is induced by $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $a\in K$ and $s\in C$ are represented by sections over $V$ and $f^{-1}V$ after intersecting neighbourhoods, [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] computes $a\cdot s$ by their sectionwise product. Taking its germ at $\eta_X$ gives $c(a\cdot s)=f^*(a)c(s)$, because $f^*$ is exactly the generic stalk map [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Thus $c$ is $K$-linear with precisely the scalar action stipulated in the statement. The image of a $K$-basis under a linear isomorphism is a basis, so $\dim_K C=\dim_K L=[k(X):f^*k(Y)]$, finite by Step 2.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q157-045e84999 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all eight steps in full, together with every cited statement and the sources Stacks 0BET (varieties.tex:10477) and 01TE (morphisms.tex:3565). The item statement is unchanged from live (still unsplit there), there are no new nodes, and the item has no re-split note. Step 1: the generic stalks are fields, so the residue fields are K and L; applying 0A21(6) to X and Y and the 030H tower gives trdeg_K L = 0 because g is finite. Step 2: the lft affine-pairs node with W⊆f^{-1}V gives L = K(b_i), and 09GH makes the extension finite. Step 3: the 01TE trf node needs lft and a finite residue extension, both of which hold; with the subspace topology on the fibre, the generic fibre is {η_X}. Step 4: 01T6 makes X and Y Noetherian, 01OY plus qcqs-permanence (1) makes f quasi-separated, and finite type makes it quasi-compact; 02NW then gives a dense open U ∋ η_Y. Step 5: finite implies affine, so the affine-vanishing node applies. Its R^p is pqf-def-cohomology, which is built on def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image and the bounded-below-injectives K-injective node, so it is the same notion as the item's R^p; open restriction then has no hypotheses. Steps 6-8 are elementary and correct: the closed map gives f^{-1}V_W ⊆ W, the germ map is bijective, and K-linearity comes from f^♯ and the stalk action. Small cases checked: g=0, the identity, a point blow-up, Frobenius on 𝔸¹, the normalization of a cusp. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre is plain Stacks 01TE scheme theory. Its 12-node closure contains no other trace-formula or Poincaré node, so it is not part of either assumption, and the same flag was accepted before. The unit's own lem-sfb-scheme-algebraic-residue-closed-point needs {s} closed, so it does not apply here. No duplicate exists in the DAG. I accept the 12 general algebraic-geometry tool_uses. No SGA is cited. No fixes.
